response.sql: WITH matched AS (SELECT o.timespan AS bucket, r.riskandmarginpivot FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = r.ordervault), buckets AS (SELECT bucket, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM matched GROUP BY bucket), shares AS (SELECT bucket, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM buckets), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), kept AS (SELECT s.cnt, s.share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share) SELECT SUM(k.cnt) AS total_count, AVG(k.share) AS avg_kept_share, AVG(k.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess_share FROM kept k CROSS JOIN avg_share a;

assumptions.assumption: Risk/margin rows with no matching order are dropped by the inner join, and each risk/margin row is counted once in its bucket.

A NULL orders.timespan is the 'no time in force' case; GROUP BY places all NULLs in one bucket. If the data instead uses an empty string or other sentinel for this case, that sentinel would need its own handling.
orders.recordvault is unique, as the documentation says. The schema does not enforce this, so a duplicate would multiply matched rows and inflate counts.
